curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-abel: Abel runs close-set, like beads on a thread, with open-mouthed curves and no sparkle at all. Red Hat Display adds marker-bold lines, say for a terminal theme.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-alegreya-s: Alegreya Sans has a broad g and a, with letters squeezed close, under a marker-plain Red Hat Display. Alegreya Sans keeps a long block of text steady and friendly, maybe beside a coffee roaster logo.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-assistant: Red Hat Display draws every letter with one width of stroke, like a bent wire, bold and contemporary. And Assistant keeps its mouths open below, so its size can stay modest for, say, demo video title cards.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-asul: Red Hat Display is built from dowel-like stems and bent arcs, which gives it a bold, blunt presence. Asul has a quiet tug between heavier verticals and lighter horizontals, so it handles the refined detail, say for a boutique hotel logo.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-b612: Blunt marker lines meet a quiet workhorse. Make Red Hat Display small and its bold, wire-like lines lose their presence, while B612 set large starts to feel plain and a bit stiff.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-belleza: Bent-wire lettering over a body with a gentle weight gradient and tiny gaps between glyphs. Shrink Red Hat Display and its bold character fades, while Belleza at large sizes shows its slivers of space.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-castoro: Marker-blunt, round-tipped strokes run from end to end. Castoro puts thread-thin lines next to heavy ones, which makes the two feel like different centuries sharing a page, and it is made for short stretches of reading.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-gloock: Wire-bent curves up top, never thinning at the spine. Gloock's thick curves taper to almost nothing, so beside Red Hat Display it feels dramatic and editorial, say for an esports team logo, and better for brief copy.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-playfair: Dignified, with a pale thread running between black stems. Red Hat Display does plain, constant-width boldness best, while Playfair does the thick-and-hairline contrast, maybe for an accounting firm wordmark.
curated-fs-red-hat-display-gf-pt-sans-na: PT Sans Narrow reads tightly kerned and approachable, with strokes that hold their width from stem to curve, made for short stretches of reading. Red Hat Display does bold, marker-plain headlines best (a law firm monogram, perhaps), while PT Sans Narrow does compact text.
